title: A methanogen hydrolase reveals the structure of archaeal peptidoglycan
title_zh: 甲烷古菌水解酶揭示古菌肽聚糖结构
abstract: Peptidoglycan (PG) is a near-universal and essential feature of bacterial cell walls and a major antimicrobial target1. Although archaea generally lack PG2, a PG-like polymer (pseudomurein or archaeal PG) was described decades ago in a major clade of methanogenic archaea3–8, yet it has remained poorly characterized, owing to the lack of dedicated analytical tools. Here we identify and characterize ArmA from Methanobrevibacter smithii, a dominant member of the human gut microbiome9, as the first glycosyl hydrolase specific for archaeal PG. ArmA-mediated digestion reveals an unexpected architecture that revises the prevailing model of archaeal PG. The glycan backbone comprises N-acetylglucosamine/N-acetylgalactosamine linked to a previously undescribed sugar, which we name N-acetylarmosamine. Glycan strands alternate β(1,4) and β(1,3) linkages, and the stem peptide is attached by means of an amide bond to the N-acetylarmosamine succinyl group. ArmA has dual enzymatic activity, cleaving both glycosidic linkages and peptide crosslinks. Phylogenetic analyses show that ArmA homologues are restricted to PG-bearing archaea, and we confirm activity across diverse methanogens. We further demonstrate that ArmA is required to complete cytokinesis, cleaving archaeal PG at the site of cell division. Together, these findings overturn a 50-year-old paradigm on archaeal PG structure and establish ArmA as a critical tool that parallels the impact of muramidases in bacteria, enabling biochemical and genetic interrogation of methanogen cell-wall biology. Finally, given the ecological and biotechnological importance of methanogens10,11, our results open new avenues for targeted intervention. ArmA from Methanobrevibacter smithii, a dominant member of the human gut microbiome, is identified and characterized as a glycosyl hydrolase specific for cleaving the cell wall of methanogens, revealing an unsuspected chemical structure of archaeal peptidoglycan that includes a previously unidentified sugar.
abstract_zh: 肽聚糖（PG）是细菌细胞壕的近乎普遍且必不可少的特征，是主要的抗菌靶点1。虽然古菌通常缺乏PG2，但几十年前在甲烷古菌一个主要类群中描述了类似PG的聚合物（假肽聚糖或古菌PG）3–8，然而由于缺乏专用的分析工具，其特征一直知之甚少。在这里，我们鉴定并表征了来自人类肠道微生物群中占主导地位的甲烷沼气古菌甲烷沼气古菌的ArmA，作为专门针对古菌PG的第一个糖苷水解酶。ArmA介导的消化揭示了出人意料的结构，修订了目前关于古菌PG的主流模型。糖聚合物骨干由N-乙酰葡萄糖胺/N-乙酰半乳糖胺与我们命名为N-乙酰阿莫糖的此前未描述的糖连接而成。糖链交替具有β(1,4)和β(1,3)连接，肽链通过酰胺键连接到N-乙酰阿莫糖琥珀酸基团上。ArmA具有双酶活性，可水解糖苷键和肽交联。系统发育分析显示，ArmA同源物仅限于携带PG的古菌，且我们在多样化的甲烷古菌中证实了其活性。此外，我们进一步证明ArmA对于完成细胞分裂是必需的，它在细胞分裂部位切割古菌PG。总之，这些发现推翻了关于古菌PG结构的50年老观点，确立ArmA作为关键工具的重要性，其影响力可与细菌中的 muramidases 相提并论，从而实现对甲烷古菌细胞壁生物学的生化和遗传学研究。最后，考虑到甲烷古菌的生态和生物技术重要性10,11，我们的研究成果开辟了针对性干预的新途径。ArmA来自甲烷沼气古菌甲烷沼气古菌，是人类肠道微生物群中占主导地位的成员，被鉴定并表征为专门水解甲烷古菌细胞壁的糖苷水解酶，揭示了古菌肽聚糖意想不到的化学结构，其中包括一种此前未被识别的糖。
